summary: Explore the Moon Astro World is a multilingual (Turkish/English), 3D educational space-game platform created for the NASA Space Apps Challenge to introduce children and teens to space science. It is a no-installation browser game accessible on all phones, tablets and computers that uses touch and keyboard controls and switches to lower graphics on slow computers. It includes large games like Mission Design Center (create a real mission with an engineering model), Lunar Greenhouse Base, Moon Base Commander, Lunar Colony, Moon Explorer, Rover Mission, Moon Landing and Space Station along with a Moon Play Park of 10 small games. These games are integrated into a seven-stage "Space Mission" campaign – design, land, rover, station, greenhouse, commander, colony – to tell a single story in which every section makes power, water, oxygen, science and fuel to build the next. Learning features include 166 info cards, a 125-question quiz, Trophy Room, weekly league, daily quests, a printable commander certificate, and a parent panel. Progress is saved on-device; tests use real equations for consistency (Tsiolkovsky rocket equation, eclipse/battery power, data downlink, panel ageing). The model is based on NASA guides (Design & Develop Science Missions, JPL CML, GMAT) and validated by 3,807 design attempts, 8,181 computer tests, 0 failures. New online server software is in progress to make the games online and share a single experience across different devices.
details:
Explore the Moon Astro World is a new bilingual (Turkish/English) learning platform with large, interactive 3D space games, developed for NASA Space Apps Challenge by using Moon Astro World, asteroids, and related facts, and hosted for children, teenagers, teachers and science-communication participants. It runs completely in a browser, with no installs, downloads or accounts needed. It is reactive, so desktop, tablet and phone will all experience the same game in terms of interactivity and controls (keyboard & controller, multi-touch), with automatic graphics quality reductions for devices where lag is detected. The front-end is built with Vite 5 using React 18 + React Router 6 + three.js 0.169 + Tailwind CSS 3.4, in a single, self-contained HTML file 2.3 MB.

They offer 8 main games – Mission Design Center (the flagship: plan a complete space mission with a real engineering model), Lunar Greenhouse Base (a 7-mission 3D science adventure), Moon Base Commander (a 5-chapter 3D story game), Lunar Colony (3D colony with 36 buildings), Moon Explorer (a big open world with 56 missions), Rover Mission (3D driving, 12 samples to find), Moon Landing (10 chapters x 3 difficulty levels) and Space Station (a 12-room puzzle), plus a Moon Play Park with 10 mini games. These are connected by a 7-phase "Space Mission" campaign: mission design - landing – rover – station – greenhouse – commander – colony - where each completed module yields resources (energy, water, oxygen, science and fuel) and becomes the starting point for the next node.

The flagship module, The Mission Design Center, is based on validated data: 9 mission objectives, with real costs and schedules 33 science instruments in 15 science instrument groups 9 spacecraft subsystems 6 orbits: LEO, SSO, GEO, lunar polar, L1, L2 6 launch vehicles, 15 in-flight events + 3 in-design events 45 discovery cards, 22 real-mission analogues. Its simulations are based on real equations: the Tsiolkovsky rocket equation, eclipse/battery power, data downlink and solar-panel ageing; and the whole model is documented in a public open model card in line with NASA standards (Design & Develop Science Missions, JPL CML, GMAT). It is verified by an automated self-test of 3,807 designs, with 8,181 checks (0 failures), and is labelled code-verified, not NASA approved.

Near the games, the site has 166 flip info cards, a 125 question quiz across 8 topics, a Trophy Room with 43 star slots and 12 badges, a weekly league of 9 ranks, daily quests, a weekly tournament, a print-ready commander certificate, a leaderboard, and a math-gated parent panel with play time and progress information. All progress is saved locally on the device (localStorage, no accounts, nothing sent anywhere). Online server infrastructure is in the works to host the games online and synchronize across devices.
